elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The carve-out applies only to a “financially responsible affiliate,” imposing a qualification absent from the preferred position. Written notice is also required, although that does not itself constitute consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a successor in interest by way of merger, subject to written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in an acquisition without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a successor in interest by way of acquisition, subject to written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a successor in interest through a sale of all or substantially all of its assets, subject to written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires TrueLink to obtain Client’s prior written approval, and the assignment carve-out is expressly limited to assignments by Client.

elements.element: Customer consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the required approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that TrueLink shall not assign or transfer the Agreement to any competitor of Client.

elements.element: Customer’s change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that a change of control of Client shall not give TrueLink any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent, subject to written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to a successor in interest through merger, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all assets, provided it gives TrueLink written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent, subject to written notice to Customer.
elements.evidence: No successor carve-out is provided for TrueLink; TrueLink remains subject to Client’s prior written approval.

elements.element: Customer may make assignments other than successor assignments with Vendor consent, and that consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Although the general approval standard is reasonable, Client may assign to a financially responsible affiliate without consent, so consent is not required for every non-successor assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may make assignments other than successor assignments with Customer consent, and that consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The general consent standard applies to TrueLink, but the absolute competitor prohibition prevents assignment to a competitor even with Client consent, making the fallback regime incomplete.

result.reason: The clause achieves most of the preferred position, including Customer M&A assignment rights, Vendor consent requirements, the competitor prohibition, and protection against termination on Customer change of control. It misses the preferred affiliate right because that right is limited to financially responsible affiliates. It also fails the fallback because Vendor has no notice-only successor right and the mutual consent regime contains asymmetric exceptions and restrictions. The drafting adds notice, reorganization, delayed-consent, suspension, and repricing terms beyond what was necessary, and the scope of “provided that” is somewhat ambiguous, though no contradiction affecting unrelated commercial terms is apparent.
